text: Kant argues that time is empirically real yet transcendentally ideal: it is the a priori form of ___ sense, valid for all objects of possible experience but not a property of things in themselves.
explanation: For Kant, time is the a priori form of inner sense — the structure through which the mind represents its own states, and thereby all appearances — which makes it empirically real yet transcendentally ideal (Critique A34/B50, A35/B52). The expected word is 'inner.' Space, by contrast, is the form of outer sense, whereas time conditions all appearances whatsoever.
